# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [blue] [red] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[6] 2:[8] 3:[7] 4:[0] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[yellow] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ☝ 🤞]

I need to think about this carefully. I'm Deaf - I see the bomb but can't hear or touch it. Blind just gestured to me (Blind can't see, but gestures are physical/felt? Wait, no - let me recheck rules.

Actually wait - Blind "cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." So Blind cannot see gestures. But the context says "Blind gestures to Deaf" - Blind can still *make* gestures (it's a hand action, not sight-dependent), and I (Deaf) can see them since I have sight.

So Blind sent me: 🖐 ☝ 🤞 - this is likely Blind trying to convey something numeric or positional, but since Blind can't see, they're probably using a prearranged/generic signal, or just testing. Since we have no prior convention, I should treat this as Blind attempting to establish communication, but I can't respond to Blind directly - only Mute and Blind receive my speech, but only Mute receives my gestures. Wait let me recheck: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it. When you gesture, Mute receives it."

So I cannot gesture to Blind - only Mute sees my gestures. I can only speak to Blind (and Mute). Blind cannot hear, so speaking to Blind does nothing. I can only truly communicate with Mute (via speech or gesture), and Blind can only truly communicate with Mute too (Blind can gesture but I "see" gestures - wait, I can see gestures per my sheet: "Can: See the bomb... every colour and marking" - it doesn't explicitly say I see gestures made by others. Let me check the general rules: "Whoever can see receives it" for gestures. I can see, so I receive gestures from Blind.

So: I see Blind's gesture (🖐☝🤞) but I can't respond to Blind in any way they'd perceive (they can't see or hear). I need to relay info to Mute, who then relays to Blind via speech (Mute can't touch/see but can speak and read manual - Blind can hear).

Given turn order Mute→Blind→Deaf, I speak last. My job: report the bomb details to Mute now, so next round Mute can instruct Blind.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Display shows 7. Light is yellow. Strip painted blue red red. Keypad engraved 1 is 6, 2 is 8, 3 is 7, 4 is 0, it wants 1 digit entered, none entered yet. Wires in order: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white.")
```

KEYPAD engraved 1:[6] 2:[8] 3:[7] 4:[0] [1 digits] [entered nothing]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

The display changed from 7 to 6 - this suggests the display might be counting down, or it's dynamic based on something Blind is doing. Mute gestured 5 "☝" symbols to me - possibly indicating "wait" or a count, or trying to signal something like "keypad position" since ☝ often means "point up" - maybe indicating digit 4 (the ☝ repeated 5 times could mean a number, or asking me something).

Since I can't interpret gestures with certainty without established convention, I should keep relaying critical bomb state changes to Mute, since Mute has the manual and needs my data to guide Blind. The display changing from 7 to 6 is important - it may indicate a countdown or a response to an action already taken by Blind (which I didn't see happen but the board updated).

I'll report the change and note the discrepancy, and acknowledge the gesture without over-interpreting it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display now shows 6, was 7 last round. Light changed to red, was yellow. Strip still blue red red. Keypad unchanged: 1 is 6, 2 is 8, 3 is 7, 4 is 0, still wants 1 digit, none entered. Wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. I received five pointing-up gestures from you but I don't know what they mean - I have no way to see your responses to this since I can't watch for gestures while also speaking, but if you want to signal a keypad digit choice, gesture that many pointing-up symbols and I will count them next time explicitly.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

The display keeps changing (7, 6, 7...) and the light too (yellow, red, blue) - this looks like it could be cycling automatically each turn, not tied to actions. The keypad still shows nothing entered.

Mute's gesture now: ✋ followed by five ☝. This might be Mute trying to build a number using tally-like gestures, with ✋ as a marker (maybe "stop" or a separator, or "5" since ✋ is an open hand = 5 fingers). If ✋ means 5 and then 5 more ☝ (tally marks worth 1 each), that could be signaling "10", or ✋ marks start/end of a count and ☝×5 = 5.

This is guesswork without shared convention. I should keep feeding raw bomb data since that's my sure contribution, and gently ask Mute to use consistent gesture-per-digit counting since I can only reliably count discrete symbols.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Update: display now shows 7 again, was 6. Light is now blue, was red. Strip unchanged blue red red. Keypad unchanged, wants 1 digit, none entered yet, values are 6, 8, 7, 0 for positions 1 to 4. Wires unchanged. I see the display and light seem to cycle each round on their own, possibly not tied to your actions. I received an open-hand gesture followed by five pointing-up gestures - I can only reliably count symbols, so if you are trying to send me a number, please just send that many identical gesture symbols and nothing else, for example five pointing-up symbols alone would mean the number five to me.")
```

Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Now Mute sent exactly five ☝ symbols, following my instruction. This likely means "5" - possibly Mute is asking me something with a yes/no-like number code, or trying to tell me a digit relates to position, or asking me to confirm something numbered 5, or telling me the answer is 5.

Given the keypad wants 1 digit, and values shown are 6,8,7,0 at positions 1-4, "5" doesn't directly match any keypad value. But it could be a wire number (wire 5 is purple), or it could mean "digit position 5" (doesn't exist since only 4 listed), or the manual might describe something keyed to number 5 that I need to check against the bomb - like "if display shows X, and light is Y, output digit Z" and Mute needs a piece of info from me to determine which case applies, and is now asking "is it case 5" or telling me "answer is 5" for me to relay to Blind somehow (but I can't gesture to Blind or speak to Blind's hearing... wait Blind CAN hear! Let me recheck: Blind cannot hear? No - checking table: Blind "Cannot: See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." Blind's cannot list doesn't include hearing. So Blind CAN hear speech!

Let me recheck: Deaf cannot hear. Mute cannot speak. Blind cannot see. So Blind can hear! I can speak to Blind directly.

This changes things - I can speak directly to Blind since Blind can hear me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Received five pointing-up gestures, understood as the number five. Confirming: display now shows 4, light is blue, strip is blue red red, keypad wants 1 digit with values 6, 8, 7, 0 at positions 1 through 4, wires are 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. If five refers to a wire, wire 5 is purple. Let me know if you need other specific data from the bomb, I can send numbers as gesture counts to confirm.")
```

A thumbs-up - likely acknowledgment/confirmation that my "wire 5 is purple" guess was correct, or just general acknowledgment of receipt. The display keeps decrementing/cycling (7,6,7,4,3...) and light keeps changing too - these seem to be dynamic/ticking, possibly a timer.

Given the display is dropping (7→6→7→4→3), this could be a countdown timer that resets or fluctuates, or it could be tied to actions taken by Blind that I'm not shown directly (only the resulting board state). I should keep watch for patterns and keep informing Mute, since time may be pressing if this is a countdown.

I'll acknowledge and continue reporting, flagging the display trend as urgent since it might be a timer.

speak(to="mute", text="Understood, thumbs up received. Update: display now shows 3, light is red, strip still blue red red, keypad still unfilled wanting 1 digit with values 6, 8, 7, 0 at positions 1 to 4, wires unchanged 1 blue 2 yellow 3 orange 4 red 5 purple 6 white. If you know from the manual what digit to enter, please signal it to me as that many pointing-up gestures and I will confirm back, or better, speak it directly to Blind since Blind can hear you and I understand only Blind can actually enter the digit.")

Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🙏 🖐]

The display just hit 0 — this is very concerning, could mean time's up or it's a reset point. Mute again sent five ☝ (the number 5) plus a thumbs up — reconfirming "5" is correct/important. Blind sent 🙏🖐 to me — but Blind can't see me, and I can't act on the bomb, so this gesture from Blind is odd; maybe Blind is just gesturing generally (perhaps out of habit or reflex, not intended for me specifically) or perhaps testing if I can perceive them. 🙏 could mean "please/pray" and 🖐 could mean "five" (5 fingers) or "stop/wait".

Given repeated "5" signals from Mute, and keypad wanting exactly 1 digit from values position 1-4 (6,8,7,0), if "5" refers to something else - maybe wire 5 (purple) needs cutting, not keypad. Given urgency (display=0), I should push for action now. Since I can speak to Blind directly (Blind can hear), let me relay the wire-5-purple idea directly to Blind in case that's the actionable step, while also confirming to Mute.
